feedback: Written before any race of this geometry, and no earlier race exists, so this is based only on the contract and my integration choices. What I had to do: the five sensors are evenly spaced, so I used sensor-x-proportional weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. This makes the signal close to linear across the span, but it also means the outer sensors carry the most weight and will dominate once the line reaches the edge. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the controller acts on the line roughly 0.05 m before the wheels reach it; this is a lag I cannot fully remove and it is why I kept kd small. Next race, if max_error is high while line_loss_events is 0, the span is too narrow for the turns. Widen the outer sensors toward x = ±0.06 and keep the layout otherwise fixed. If line_loss_events is high, the 12 mm footprint may be missing the 25 mm tape at speed. Try sensor_size 0.016 before moving the sensors. If steering_oscillation is high, the sensors are too far ahead for the speed. Move the row back toward y = 0.03 and keep the span.
requested_changes: If the next race shows high max_error with few line losses, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 (keep 5 sensors) to cover sharper bends; this is an untested inference from the contract's 25 mm tape and the 0.04 m span.
If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero, set sensor_size to 0.016 so a single sensor covers more of the 25 mm tape at speed; the baseline 0.012 footprint is untested at speed.
If the next race shows steering_oscillation high, move the sensor row back to y = 0.03 to reduce lookahead lag; the 5 cm lookahead is untested and may be the cause.
